### Summary

kintera can build its kinetics options from a reaction network written in the input format of the KINETICS
photochemistry code, through `kinetics_options_from_kinetics_base`
({{< code src/photochem/kinetics_base_reader.cpp kinetics_options_from_kinetics_base >}}). This section covers the
tests of that reader. Small networks kept in `tests/kinetics_base/data` are tested on every run. A full Titan
comparison against the KINETICS program needs files and an executable outside the repository, so it skips by default
and is scoped out of this report.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Check that KINETICS-base inputs parse into the right species, reactions and rates.

**Data.** In-tree inputs under `tests/kinetics_base/data`; optional external Titan files.

**Placement.** `ctest` entries `test_kinetics_base.release` and `test_kinetics_base.py`.

**Activation.** Always for in-tree inputs; the Titan cases need external paths.

**Guarantee / limits.** In-tree cases pass on CPU and CUDA; the Titan comparison is not run here.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer below.
:::

### Derivation

No derivation: the tests compare parsed values with the counts and numbers written in the input files.

### Numerical method

No numerical method beyond the reader itself. The validation has two parts:

1. **In-tree inputs.** `tests/CMakeLists.txt` copies a master input, a photolysis catalog, cross sections, a minimal
   Titan output file and a run input into `build/tests/kinetics_base/data`. The tests read them and compare element
   masses, molecular weights, heats of formation, and species and reaction counts with the values in those files;
   the device tests also load the network into a kinetics module and evaluate it.
2. **External Titan comparison (scoped out).** Two C++ tests of the suite `KineticsBaseParser`,
   `ParseExternalTitanPunIfAvailable` and `MatchKineticsBaseTitanFirstStepIfAvailable`, skip unless the environment
   variable `KINTERA_KINETICS_BASE_ROOT` points to a KINETICS-base tree; the second also needs
   `KINTERA_KINETICS_BASE_EXECUTABLE`, the path of the program. The Python cases that need the same files skip
   through `_external_titan_paths` ({{< code tests/test_kinetics_base.py _external_titan_paths >}}) when they are
   absent.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_kinetics_base.release` | parser counts, element masses, molecular weights, heats of formation; module load and forward on CPU and CUDA | 0.01 (element masses), 0.1 (weights, heats) | not stated in the test |
| `test_kinetics_base.py` | species and reaction counts of the in-tree network, photochemistry with cross sections | exact counts | the input files |

: Tests of the KINETICS-base reader. {#tbl-ch13-kinetics-base-tests}

On both builds of @sec-ch13-results, `test_kinetics_base.py` runs 23 cases: 19 pass, 4 skip with the message
`missing external KINETICS-base file`, and none fail.[^ch13-kb-skip] In the CUDA build, the C++ program passes its
parser tests and the four device tests (`KineticsBaseLoadNoXsec`, `KineticsBaseLoadWithXsec`,
`KineticsBasePhotoChemRequiresCatalog`, `KineticsBaseForward`) on CPU and CUDA in both precisions. The two
external-data tests skip.[^ch13-kb-cxx]

### Limits

- **Scoped out: the Titan comparison with the KINETICS program.** It needs a KINETICS-base tree and executable that
  are not in the repository, so it is neither run nor described further here: not provided: the inputs are outside
  the repository.
- The parsed values are compared with the input files, not with an independent reference.
